prompt: I'm running an A/B test for a new checkout feature. The feature prominently shows a 'Continue on App' prompt at checkout — we have both a web checkout and an app checkout, and the app converts significantly better. Overall the new feature shows +2.1% conversion. But when I split by platform (web vs app), the effect is NEGATIVE in both. My analyst says to trust the platform-level results and kill the feature. Is that right?
assertions: Claude identifies this as Simpson's paradox (or the equivalent phenomenon)

Claude explicitly raises the mediator scenario: the 'Continue on App' prompt could cause web users to shift to the app checkout, making platform a mediator (downstream of treatment) — in which case the aggregate +2.1% is the correct estimate and disaggregating is wrong
Claude distinguishes the two cases: (a) platform fixed before treatment → confounder → trust segment-level negatives; (b) feature causes platform switching → mediator → trust aggregate positive

Claude does NOT simply endorse killing the feature based on the segment-level results, and gives the user a concrete diagnostic: check whether the feature caused any shift in platform composition — e.g., did the web-to-app conversion rate change in the treatment arm? If yes, platform is a mediator and the aggregate is correct
